text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nova Scotia fight rudeness on field, ice: Fair-play sports program proposes banning abusive players, spectators and coaches.
- Mike Harris sticks to Metro merger: Rejection in vote to bring changes.
- Alberta nurses vote 85 percent to strike: Threat bodes ill for Klein.
- Victims of sexual assaults went public, feel punished.
- Blair's wife feels heat of Tory press.
- Kruger launches bid for Scott: Tissue maker's stock tumbles on news offer, but analysts say it's the best deal available.
- Angry activist quits meeting of Laurentian Bank: Wished to avoid 'dishonour' of defeat of governance, executive pay proposals.
- Eaton's suppliers demand answers: May ask court to shed light on finances.
- CanWest raises stake in WIC to 15 percent: C$34-million move 'strategic investment' in broadcasting rival.
- Banks ahead in RRSP stakes: Along with Canada Trust, they take in C$6.43 billion in new assets in January, February.
- Kruger offers C$351-million for Scott, gives Kimberly-Clark an exit.
